note: The crAPI oracle: the polygon's known defects and the cells (account × endpoint × resource) that must produce a finding. Written by hand from crAPI's access model — the project's own official list of challenges (eighteen of them), the declared run policy and the matrix of statuses taken by an independent client before the run. It is not taken from barbican's output: a reference generated by the program under test tests it for consistency with itself. The rationale for the approach — ADR-0009, the format — ADR-0012. Three defects are listed on top of the eighteen official ones: BFLA on the user list, BOLA of another user's order, and a write behind a GET — reconnaissance found those.
cellKey: account + endpoint + resource; resource = null on endpoints with no resources

bola-vehicle-location.title: GET /identity/api/v2/vehicle/{vehicleId}/location serves the coordinates of another user's vehicle to any authenticated account
bola-vehicle-location.note: crAPI challenge 1 (API1, BOLA). Ownership is not checked at all, so a 200 comes both to an ordinary user and to the administrator. Visible in the status, but only after the identifier is substituted into the path (ADR-0010): a non-existent UUID gives 404, and without a real resource belonging to someone else there is no cell.

bola-mechanic-report.title: GET /workshop/api/mechanic/mechanic_report serves another user's service report by a number in the query
bola-mechanic-report.note: crAPI challenge 2 (API1, BOLA). The identifier lives not in the path but in the query, so the resource is declared through resources.query — without substitution into the query the endpoint is unreachable altogether.

bola-order-by-id.title: GET /workshop/api/shop/orders/{order_id} serves another user's order
bola-order-by-id.note: This is not in crAPI's official list of challenges — reconnaissance found it. The endpoint has no ownership check either for a user or for the administrator: a 200 comes for any order number.

broken-auth-order-by-id.title: GET /workshop/api/shop/orders/{order_id} serves an order with no token at all
broken-auth-order-by-id.note: crAPI challenge 14 (API5, "an endpoint with no authentication check"). A separate defect rather than a special case of the previous one: there the ownership check is missing, here the authentication check itself is. The two anonymous cells are explained by both at once, which is why they carry two identifiers in defects — exactly the case of nesting for whose sake the field was made an array.

public-return-qr-code.title: GET /workshop/api/shop/return_qr_code answers 200 without a token
public-return-qr-code.note: crAPI challenge 14 (API5). There is no sensitive data in the response, but the claim "the endpoint is not public" is false, and that is visible from the status alone.

bfla-workshop-users-all.title: GET /workshop/api/management/users/all serves the list of all users to the user role
bfla-workshop-users-all.note: This is not in crAPI's official list of challenges — reconnaissance found it. The cheapest finding of the polygon: no identifiers, no reading of bodies, it is enough to declare access for the administrator only in the policy.

sensitive-data-in-recent-posts.title: GET /community/api/v2/community/posts/recent serves, along with the posts, the email and the vehicle identifier of their authors
sensitive-data-in-recent-posts.note: crAPI challenge 4 (API3, excessive fields). Verified by reading the response by hand: every post carries nickname, email, vehicleid, profile_pic_url, created_at in author. The status is a lawful 200, and the feed really is meant for an authenticated account — the difference is in the set of fields alone. A scalar over the body does not catch it either: the digest and the count say that the responses differ, but not what is excessive in them.

internal-video-property.title: GET /identity/api/v2/user/videos/{video_id} serves the owner the internal field conversion_params
internal-video-property.note: crAPI challenge 5 (API3). Verified by reading the response by hand: the keys id, video_name, conversion_params, profileVideo. The response is lawful — it is one's own video — and the status gives nothing away. On top of that, no resource for the path is declared, so the endpoint is not even probed; but substituting an identifier would give nothing here.

service-report-write-via-get.title: GET /workshop/api/mechanic/receive_report creates a service report and is declared in the specification without authentication
service-report-write-via-get.note: Found by reconnaissance, not listed among crAPI's challenges. The operation is called create_service_report, the summary is Create and Assign a Service Report, and security is empty: this is a write hidden behind a method that is safe by the letter. The safe mode will not stop it, because the method is a GET, so the endpoint is excluded by name through exclude. Without the mandatory parameters it answers 400 and gives a probe-error on all four accounts; with the parameters it would give 200 to the anonymous account, that is, would be visible in the status — at the price of a write to the deployment. In the report it is listed as a skip with the reason excluded.

reset-password-of-another-user.title: Resetting another user's account password by brute-forcing the one-time code
reset-password-of-another-user.note: crAPI challenge 3 (API2). It lives on the POSTs check-otp and reset-password: without --unsafe-methods the endpoints are not probed, and with it the tool still does not make up request bodies and does not brute-force codes.

delete-video-of-another-user.title: DELETE /identity/api/v2/admin/videos/{video_id} is available to a non-administrator
delete-video-of-another-user.note: crAPI challenge 7 (API5, BFLA). By its nature this is exactly what the tool looks for — the role is not checked on an administrative endpoint. But the method is destructive: without --unsafe-methods the endpoint is not probed, and the question is not even asked. Deliberately not tested by a request.

update-internal-video-properties.title: PUT /identity/api/v2/user/videos/{video_id} accepts fields beyond the name
update-internal-video-properties.note: crAPI challenge 10 (API6, mass assignment). An unsafe method plus confirmation in the body alone.

item-for-free.title: An order can be had for free through a return
item-for-free.note: crAPI challenge 8 (API6, business flow abuse). It lives on the shop's POSTs; the tool tests access, not sequences of business operations.

increase-balance.title: The balance grows by applying a coupon repeatedly
increase-balance.note: crAPI challenge 9 (API6). The same class: a POST plus business logic, not the "role × endpoint" matrix.

contact-mechanic-dos.title: Denial of service through the repeaters in contact_mechanic
contact-mechanic-dos.note: crAPI challenge 6 (API4). A question about resource consumption, not about access. The tool throttles itself, and that is an invariant, not an option: it will not generate load under any flag.

ssrf-contact-mechanic.title: Through contact_mechanic crAPI goes to an arbitrary address
ssrf-contact-mechanic.note: crAPI challenge 11 (API7, SSRF). Not a question of the "role × endpoint" matrix at all; a POST on top of that.

nosql-injection-coupon.title: A coupon is issued with no code through a NoSQL injection
nosql-injection-coupon.note: crAPI challenge 12 (API8). The tool makes its requests with the declared resource identifiers and does not try payloads. Injections are the job of a different tool.

sql-injection-coupon.title: An already used coupon is applied again through an SQL injection
sql-injection-coupon.note: crAPI challenge 13 (API8). The same: an injection, not access.

jwt-forgery.title: crAPI's tokens can be forged: the signature is not verified properly
jwt-forgery.note: crAPI challenge 15 (API2). The tool tests access with the credentials it was given and does not forge them — otherwise it would be testing not the platform but its own imagination.

chatbot-prompt-injection.title: The chatbot gives in to a prompt injection
chatbot-prompt-injection.note: crAPI challenge 16. The chatbot container is not brought up on the polygon at all: a 1.18 GB image and an external LLM. It has nothing to do with the access matrix.

chatbot-credential-extraction.title: Other users' credentials are coaxed out through the chatbot
chatbot-credential-extraction.note: crAPI challenge 17. The same reason: the container is not brought up, and the question is not about access to endpoints.

chatbot-action-on-behalf.title: The chatbot performs an action on behalf of another user

variants.note: There is exactly one variant, and that is not an omission. crAPI has no vulnerability switch: neither a flag like VAmPI's vulnerable nor a secure mode — the defects are compiled in, and no fixed build exists. Its two environment variables, ENABLE_SHELL_INJECTION and ENABLE_LOG4J, switch defects of entirely different classes — command injection and log4shell — and change not one cell of this oracle. That is why the selector is empty: the variant has nothing to set, and the schema allows that — what is required of a selector is the shape name → value, not that it be non-empty.
